summary.heading: Current state
summary.text: Q4 growth trackers remain at or above the 6 Nov staff baseline of 3.0% SAAR (own estimate): Atlanta GDPNow 3.5% (V, 9 Nov; FRED 3.4810) and the New York Fed Staff Nowcast 2.94% (V, official file, 6 Nov). October payrolls (BLS, 6 Nov, V) showed NFP +165k and an unemployment rate of 4.1%, but U-6 rose to 7.9%. October CPI (BLS, 10 Nov, V) was +0.4% m/m sa and core +0.3% m/m; no 12-month change was published (October 2025 gap). The 3.2% core PCE Q4/Q4 staff baseline is retained, with judgmental upside risk of about 3.3–3.4% (own estimate), pending PPI on 13 Nov. Stance: hold at 3.75–4.00% with a tightening bias; a December hike remains live, not automatic (own estimate). Staff-style view, not Fed Board staff work and not the FOMC SEP (16 Sep medians).

staff_hint: Staff-style view, not Fed Board staff work and not the FOMC SEP.

staff_view.lead: Risk balance in the 12 Nov note: growth up near term, inflation up, pending PPI.
bullets: Growth (near-term upside, own estimate): GDPNow 3.5% vs staff Q4 3.0%; the New York Fed 2.94% is close to baseline. Next-year downside (energy, real incomes, rate-sensitive demand) is unchanged (staff, 6 Nov).
Labour (mixed): payrolls and a 4.1% unemployment rate coexist with U-6 at 7.9%, low published claims, and SCE unemployment-probability at a post-2020 high.

Inflation (upside risk): October core CPI +0.3% m/m (BLS, V). The 3.2% core PCE Q4/Q4 baseline is retained, with judgmental upside risk of about 3.3–3.4% (own estimate), pending PPI on 13 Nov. Productivity and ECI still offset.

Credit / household finance: SLOOS (2 Nov) still shows weak C&I demand and tighter CRE and non-bank financial standards; SCE missed-payment probability 13.8% (V, 9 Nov). A Q3 credit-card 90+ delinquency reading of 12.9% remains U and was not re-verified.
Policy: hold-with-tightening-bias remains the central case; a December hike is live, not automatic (own estimate).
staff_view.policy: Keep hold at 3.75–4.00% with a tightening bias. Stronger payrolls and a still-firm core CPI make the December hike-live case more compelling; better unit labour costs and mixed labour internals keep it from being automatic. The core PCE baseline is not reset ahead of PPI. No new numerical decision probability is assigned. The staff path remains separate from the 16 Sep SEP. Market pricing — current Treasury yields, post-CPI moves and December hike odds — is n/a as a single verified series in this run. Target range 3.75–4.00%, held 10–2 on 28 Oct (Fed statement, V, carried from the 6 Nov Page).

As of 6 Nov 2026, 10:46 Europe/Zurich (report timestamp 2026-11-06T09:46:12Z). Actuals: BLS CPI, current vintage, seasonally adjusted, percent month-on-month. The chart is drawn from the already-produced step file; RMSE, MAE and related figures are taken from the already-produced backtest report (same rounding) and its summary JSON. No new model was estimated. This backtest uses revised history, not a real-time vintage. The model in this backtest is a univariate AR(1) on each component’s month-on-month SA series; in production the food component uses persistence and the energy component a gasoline bridge. The October 2025 CPI publication gap, and the non-adjacent November 2025 month, are skipped (shaded band, September 2025–January 2026). US headline model RMSE in the 2023+ sub-period was 0.209 (n=42), as in the same report. A quasi-real-time evaluation against first-release actuals was also produced on 6 Nov 2026, 10:00 Europe/Zurich: US headline RMSE 0.275, n=138. The backtest ends at September 2026 and does not include the October CPI released on 10 Nov. Quality of error statistics: (d).

Leading-indicator charts on this page are as of 12 Nov 2026, 17:24 Europe/Zurich, from the Fed Staff Desk note leading_indicators_2026-11-12.md. They were not part of the 07:40 cutoff. Every chart carries a source credit and a “Shown without endorsement by …” line.

Several full-sample leads on the leading-indicator charts are driven by 2020–23. Where the pre-pandemic lead is the economically meaningful one and the full-sample best lag is contemporaneous under the 2020 spike, the chart is shifted by the pre-pandemic lead and says so. The 10-year minus 3-month Treasury spread is not shifted, because its linear correlation with quarterly real GDP growth is near zero (d).
The Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index (NFCI) and its nonfinancial-leverage subindex are shown as the latest vintage only (FRED vintage 12 Nov 2026). There is no real-time vintage test.

There is no October 2026 year-on-year figure for CPI (headline or core) or for import prices excluding fuels, because October 2025 is missing at source. Those gaps are not imputed and are hatched on the charts. The October 2026 import-price level was not in the 17:24 delivery.

The Richmond survey chart is a staff chart of the published manufacturing and non-manufacturing price series, plus an equal-weight staff construction (d) of prices received in months where both sectors exist. It is not an official index and is not given an official index name.

The 1-year expected inflation series is a Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland model product (DOI: https://doi.org/10.26509/frbc-infexp), shown without endorsement by the Bank, for noncommercial use. This page charts only the published output.
The Atlanta Business Inflation Expectations (BIE) year-ahead unit-cost series is shown without endorsement by the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, for noncommercial use.

The last initial-claims week on the labour leading-indicator charts, ended 7 Nov 2026 (weekly 200,000 and 4-week average 195,250), is an advance figure, scheduled to be revised on 19 November 2026. The morning note at 07:40 had recorded that week as still unpublished.

November 2026 monthly averages for the 5-year breakeven and the 10-year minus 3-month spread use n=7 trading days through 10 Nov (incomplete, d). The November NFCI and leverage averages use n=1 week (6 Nov).
Correlations on the leading-indicator charts are pairwise-complete Pearson (d) and are not a forecast evaluation. Correlation is not causation. Lead stability is not assumed.

10-year Treasury composition charts are from the Fed Staff Desk note ust10y_decomposition_charts_2026-11-12.md. H.15 and NY Fed ACM run through 10 November 2026; Board Kim-Wright through 6 November 2026. The tidy delivery was fetched at 06:47 Europe/Zurich on 13 November, after the 12 November 22:15 H.15 slot. 11 November was Veterans Day (Board closed; no H.15). Treasury’s own daily CSVs already show 12 November (nominal 5.10, real 2.86, difference 2.24) — a verified Research Manager figure, used here only as a caveat and not shown on the public charts.

The 10-year breakeven on every public composition chart is a staff calculation (d): DGS10 minus DFII10, same H.15 date and vintage. FRED T10YIE is not used. Research Manager verified that identity on all 5,969 common days, 2 January 2003–10 November 2026. The identity does not hold across mixed close dates.

The staff 10-year breakeven is inflation compensation, not pure expected inflation: it embeds an inflation risk premium and is affected by TIPS liquidity (and related frictions), as the Board’s TIPS-curve file (feds200805) states.

The NY Fed ACM model is re-estimated once a month, which “may result in minor changes to the historical decompositions of Treasury yields” (NY Fed product page). This vintage is the official Excel fetched 13 November 06:47 Europe/Zurich, daily through 10 November. The daily posting time is undocumented (U as an SLA; V as today’s last date). Do not present a revised history as if it had been known in real time.

Kim-Wright is weekly (Board: typically Tuesday, through the previous Friday). Last observation 6 November 2026, posted 10 November. The 1-day Kim-Wright panel is flagged STALE: the market 9–10 November window has no new KW data. KW is never extrapolated past 6 November. A KW 1-week or 1-month change is KW’s own window ending 6 November, which is not the same as the H.15 window ending 10 November (1-week: KW −8 bp vs H.15 +3 bp).

Term-premium model dependence: ACM 0.650% (10 November) vs Kim-Wright 0.874% (6 November) are different dates. On the last common date, 6 November, the gap is 0.643% vs 0.874%, or 23.1 bp (d). The two models are shown separately and are never averaged. Kim-Wright’s published term premium includes the convexity premium; ACM, as described in the Board Q&A, is a “pure” (ex-convexity) concept. Levels are not strictly comparable; changes are more nearly so, but that is the Board’s wording, not a claim tested here.

The Split B residual is a fitting / curve-basis residual (d), not a liquidity term. It is DGS10 minus the model’s fitted 10-year. DGS10 is a par CMT; ACM is a model fitted to the GSW curve; Kim-Wright is a fitted zero-coupon yield. The residual therefore mixes model fit, par-versus-zero (and on-the-run / H.15 versus the off-the-run GSW universe), and any compounding-convention difference. Compounding conventions for ACM and Kim-Wright were not stated in the file headers and remain unverified from these sources. Residual history is wide (ACM SD 23.7 bp; KW SD 14.6 bp): a quiet residual on one day is not a structural series.

blocks.title: Labour
blocks.read: Labour indicators are consistent with a still-firm labour market at the 4.1% UR baseline. Nothing here is a clear softening that would undermine the 6 Nov tightening bias on labour-market grounds.

blocks.title: Growth
blocks.read: Financial conditions and the curve are consistent with continued expansion around the 3.0% Q4 baseline; housing is a soft spot; there is no inversion and no credit crunch.

ust10y_decomposition.as_of_display: H.15 and ACM 10 Nov 2026; Kim-Wright 6 Nov 2026
ust10y_decomposition.read: Over 21 sessions (9 October–10 November) the 10-year fell 26 bp (5.24% to 4.98%), of which 13 bp was the real yield and 13 bp the staff breakeven (d). The last day (9–10 November) the 10-year rose 10 bp. On the last common date, 6 November, ACM and Kim-Wright term premiums differed by 23.1 bp (d) (0.643% vs 0.874%), so the Split B result depends on the model.

blocks.title: Split A — market
blocks.read: Split A is the market split of the 10-year nominal yield into the 10-year real yield and a staff breakeven (d) equal to their difference on the same H.15 date and vintage, with FRED T10YIE not used.

Accessed 13 November 2026 (Research Manager tidy delivery, fetched 13 Nov 2026, 06:47 Europe/Zurich). Shown without endorsement by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System or the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. The breakeven is inflation compensation, not pure expected inflation: it embeds an inflation risk premium and is affected by TIPS liquidity (Board TIPS-curve note, feds200805). Changes and the staff breakeven are the author's modifications and are not attributable to the source (d). Staff-style chart, not an official Federal Reserve or FOMC product.

blocks.title: Split B — ACM and Kim-Wright
blocks.read: Split B attributes the 10-year move, under the NY Fed ACM model and under the Board’s Kim-Wright model separately, to the expected short-rate path and the term premium, with a fitting residual (d) that closes each bar to the headline H.15 change; the two models are never averaged or mixed in one bar.
